items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: I never met Pompous Celestine to La New Orleans Jazz Club down here, and Miss Menville introduced me to him.

ctx.x: Did you ever see Jelly Roll Martin?

No, I never knew him. I never met him. In fact, I never knew Joe Oliver. I never met Pompous Celestine to La New Orleans Jazz Club down here, and Miss Menville introduced me to him. And she asked him, was this one of the men who used to sit down and listen to you? He said, no, ma'am. I never seen this man in my life before. I had already told her I never met him, but she didn't believe it, but she tried to put me on the spot. But that Negro had more honesty and truthfulness in his body than Miss Menville has in…
Was Celestine playing when you were a young man?

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: And there was Oscar Papaselestine too, who is still playing music that the tourists come to New Orleans to hear.

ctx.x: Pioneer of jazz wins recognition, New Orleans, editor from New Orleans States. It was gratifying to read in your paper on February 27th the article on Nick LaRocca, famous leader of the original Dixieland jazz band. He deserves the honor accorded him and his band by the Jazz Club of England whose leader, Marcus O'Donoghau visited our sea last summer. If Mr. LaRocca accepts this invitation, and I hope he does, I'm sure he will mention some of the other bands that played jazz at that time. Tom Brown, who took his…

I'd like to comment on the dates that she has here to show you she was eaten up, taken in by this communist propaganda. I wish you'd hear this tape recorder. Buddy Bolin, Freddie Kepler, George Pequet left here in 1911. In 1906, by the things that I have in my hand, from Louisiana State Mental Hospital at Jackson, Louisiana, Bolin was incarcerated in there in 1906. He couldn't have played with them. And I've told you when these Negroes came it was 1917. Clarence Williams, he says, left here around 1911 or 13.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: I thought it was Celestine invented that.

ctx.x: We used to have swing sessions every morning around 3 o'clock after the boys got through with their work and each man would do his bit. Quote, the first hot band to leave from the South and introduce swing music was the Creole Jazz Band, unquote, says Mr. Williams. Quote, following the Dixieland Jazz Band, which recorded Livery Stable Blues and Tiger Ray, which swept the country. The Creole Band was colored and the Dixieland Band was white and they used to play across the street from each other and used to sit in…
I thought it was Celestine invented that. That's what they said, Celestine invented that. Clyde McCoy used it. Now King Oliver invented it.

Go ahead. The man who took it from King Oliver and added the plunger was Johnny Dunn, who was with Mamie Smith's Jazz Hounds and Lou Leslie's Plantation Review. It's a continuation all of the same quote. The first recording bands were the Dixieland Jazz Band. Go ahead. W.C. Smith... He played no jazz. I wonder who W.C. Smith is. Could that be Joseph Smith?
